stem:
Meera is doing her science homework at home in Pune. She takes two bar magnets. She brings the North pole of the first magnet close to the South pole of the second magnet, without letting them touch.
What will happen to the two poles?

options.text: The poles will attract each other, because a North pole and a South pole are unlike poles.
The poles will repel each other, because two magnet poles always push each other away.
The poles will repel each other, because both magnets are made of the same metal.
Nothing will happen, because the poles do not touch each other.

teacher.key_rationale: Unlike poles (N and S) attract, so A is correct. B and C trap the misconception that magnet poles always repel; D traps the idea that contact is needed for a magnetic force.
